title: The gases and compounds that can be in an atmosphere: identity, phase points, heat capacity, Rayleigh scattering (GEN.410)
sources: chemicals 1.5.2 (heos_constants, critical, triple and vapour-pressure tables), thermo 0.6.1, periodictable 2.1.0, cantera nasa_gas.yaml, NIST WebBook and NIST fluid saturation tables, Yaws and CRC values as tagged in part 01
He et al. 2021, ACP 21, 14927 (N2O, CH4, CO2, O2 refractivity); Peck and Huang 1977; Mansfield and Peck; Bideau-Mehu et al.; Cuthbertson; Allen/Cox; NIST CCCBDB polarizabilities as read in part 02
licence_note: Boss, 2026-10-17, 2:35 PM EDT: every paper and dataset acquired is usable; the raw tables are not redistributed and the licence column is a record. NIST SRD is copyrighted (permission noted in body-composition part G4); PubChem and USGS are public domain; 'open' means none was found.
notes: Each block of a row has its own status word from the research part (DATA, COMPUTED, READ, 2ND-HAND, NOT REACHED); `state` and `limit` are the row's source state in the vocabulary of GEN.472. The molar mass in the file is the research part's, kept for the audit; the loader computes the working value from `physics.elements` (GEN.438). Rayleigh sigma is per molecule in cm2; `reference_temperature_k` is the temperature the refractivity fit was made at (GEN.408).

gases.name: water vapor

rayleigh.research_note: report gives n - 1 = 2.362e-4 at 550 nm with unknown reference temperature: n-based sigma is 3.11e-27 (if 288.15 K) or 2.80e-27 (if 273.15 K); the generic formula with alpha = 1.501 A^3 gives 3.38e-27, 9 to 21 percent above. Use the report value
rayleigh.note: generic polarizability route (alpha 1.501 A^3), because the refractivity n - 1 = 2.362e-4 at 550 nm has no known reference temperature: n-based sigma(550) is 3.11e-27 if 288.15 K or 2.80e-27 if 273.15 K, so the generic value is 9 to 21 percent above; F_K 1.0010 from the vapor depolarization 2.99e-4 (linear), not the liquid's 0.17
rayleigh.limit: reference temperature of the refractivity unknown: the generic value is 9 to 21 percent above the n-based 3.11e-27 or 2.80e-27 at 550 nm
